contractRequests: WP-01 internal/config/diag/diag.go Nearest and osa: bound the cost. (1) Replace osa with a banded optimal string alignment that is capped at the distance limit (at most 3). It should remove the common prefix and suffix, keep three rows of 2*limit+1 cells, stop once two consecutive rows exceed the limit, and let each later candidate's limit drop to bestD-1, since candidates come in byte order. That is O(len) time and O(1) memory, against today's (len(a)+1)*(len(b)+1) ints. (2) Replace the strings.EqualFold pass over every candidate with a simple-fold-key map, built once per candidate list or at least restricted to candidates with the input's rune count, so the pass reads O(len(input)) instead of the summed candidate bytes. internal/config/subst/hint.go implements exactly this and is proven equal to diag.Nearest by TestHintsMatchNearest and FuzzHints; once diag.Nearest is bounded, subst can call it again behind its memo. Every other Nearest caller (kind hints and the like) gets the same bound.

01-config-load.md requirement 6 (Limits): add `MaxOutputBytes` 64 MiB (target, proposed; owner decision). It is the text substitution writes in one render: the new text of every scalar holding `${` that it rewrites, values, defaults, literal parts and unescaped `$${` alike. Passing it is RZ-CFG-001 "substitution writes more than N bytes of text in one render", with no file, line or resource. Requirement 54 and J row 003 should say the bounded-heap rule also covers substitution amplification (k uses of a v-byte variable write k*v bytes). Implemented as subst.Options.MaxOutputBytes / DefaultMaxOutputBytes.

00-architecture.md section 3 stage table (row E, about line 6650) and the paragraph at about line 6661: stage E also raises RZ-CFG-001, for the substituted-output limit (subst.CodeLimit, Substituter.LimitDiagnostic), besides 005, 007, 010, 011 and 013.

01-config-load.md requirement 28: after "`$${` is still unescaped there", add "except in mapping keys and in `apiVersion`, `kind` and `metadata.name`, where requirement 16 makes any `${`, `$${` included, RZ-CFG-011; these are never substituted or unescaped (requirement 27)". subst implements this reading.

01-config-load.md J row 013 (owner decision, recorded reading): both credential rules read the text written in the Bundle. That is a scalar's literal text with escapes resolved, plus every `${NAME:-default}`'s default whether taken or not, cut into runs at each `${NAME}` without a default. A variable's value is never read, and the result is the same whether substitution succeeds or an error leaves the authored text. A headers `set[].value` for authorization, proxy-authorization, cookie or x-api-key is a literal when a run holds a letter or digit, after removing a leading `Bearer ` or `Basic ` scheme (any case) from the run at the start; it is also a literal when no expression takes its text from the variable source. Alternative left to the owner: also flag credentials in substituted variable values (the old behavior, which made the result depend on the Environment).

01-config-load.md requirements 25 and 27 (owner decision): a dispatch member holding a `${VAR}` expression (a Policy `spec.type` of `${T}`) selects no if/then branch at stage D, because overlays merge before substitution. That has three consequences: (1) composite members merge as free content (keyed lists replaced whole; an overlay `$patch` inside is RZ-CFG-005); (2) CheckBase reports a base `$patch` inside such a Policy's `config.schema` as RZ-CFG-006; (3) an overlay `spec.type: ${T}` over a base `validation.json-schema` Policy is a changed dispatch, so a base `$patch` in `config.schema` is RZ-CFG-005. All three would be unnecessary if `T` names `validation.json-schema`. Options: (a) keep and state the rule; (b) substitute dispatch members before stage D; (c) treat an unresolved dispatch as unknown and defer `$patch` checks under it until after substitution.
deviations: Finding 2: diag.Nearest (WP-01) is still quadratic, and long HintNames could still reach that one-call cost, so a memo plus length skip would not have closed the finding. subst therefore no longer calls diag.Nearest: it computes the same answer locally in internal/config/subst/hint.go with bounded cost. Equality is proven by TestHintsMatchNearest and FuzzHints, and a contract request asks diag to adopt the same algorithm. The suggested memo (per Substituter, under a lock) and the skip of names longer than the longest entry plus 3 are both included.

Finding 3: subst reports the output limit itself as RZ-CFG-001 (CodeLimit, LimitDiagnostic) instead of returning a diagnostic for the caller to convert. RZ-CFG-001 is the registered code for 01 req 6 limits, and determinism requires the diagnostic to have the same text whichever resource trips it, so it carries no location, resource or path. The 64 MiB default is a proposal filed as a contract request.

The hints for apiVersion and kind on the no-schema path, and for metadata.name, no longer suggest `$${`, which is no escape there. This is a behavior change for the same root cause, filed against 01 req 28.

The TestCredentialWarnings rows that expected such warnings were renamed and flipped. The alternative of also flagging rendered values is left to the owner in the J row 013 contract request.
